title: Rotting Oranges
statement: You get a grid. 0 is an empty cell, 1 is a fresh orange and 2 is a rotten one. Every minute, each fresh orange that touches a rotten one (up, down, left or right) becomes rotten. Return the number of minutes until no fresh orange is left, or -1 if some fresh orange can never rot.

example.caption: One rotten orange in the corner. The rot spreads outward one step each minute, and the last orange rots at minute 4.

idea.sentence: Put every rotten orange in a queue at once. Each pass over the queue rots all their fresh neighbours together, and one pass is one minute.

jargon.plain: Breadth-first search that starts from many cells at the same time. It spreads in rings, so a cell is reached by whichever start is closest.
One ring of the spread. Here, everything that rots in the same minute.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the grid as rows of 0, 1 and 2, e.g. [[2,1,1],[1,1,0]]

vars.meaning: number of cells in the grid (rows times columns)

compare.bruteLabel: Re-scan the whole grid every minute
compare.optimalLabel: Queue of rotten oranges, each handled once

rows.name: Scan the grid each minute
rows.note: Every minute you look at all n cells to find rotten ones. A long chain needs about n minutes.

rows.name: Multi-source BFS
rows.note: Each orange joins the queue once, when it rots, and is processed once. Space is the grid copy and the queue.

fast.takeaway: The queue holds only the oranges that can spread right now. Looking at those instead of the whole grid is what saves the work.

stages.title: Queue all rotten
stages.note: Queue every rotten orange as a starting point, and count the fresh ones. All sources begin at minute 0.

stages.title: One wave = one minute
stages.note: Rot every fresh neighbour of the current queue and make those the next queue. Then add one minute.

stages.title: Check what is left
stages.note: If no fresh orange is left, return the minutes. If some remain, nothing can reach them, so return -1.

edges.title: No fresh oranges
edges.why: Nothing needs to rot. The loop stops at once, so no minute is counted.

edges.title: Fresh but no rotten
edges.why: The queue starts empty, so nothing can spread. A fresh orange remains.

edges.title: Walled-off orange
edges.why: An empty cell blocks the rot. The fresh orange behind it is never reached.

edges.title: Empty grid
edges.why: No cells, no fresh oranges, nothing to do. Do not read the first row before checking it exists.

gotchas.text: Copy each row with oranges.map(row => [...row]). A shallow copy such as [...oranges] still shares the row arrays, so rotting a cell would change the caller's grid.
Do not count a minute for the last wave if no fresh orange remains. The loop condition queue.length > 0 && fresh > 0 stops right after the minute in which the last fresh one rots.
append([]int(nil), row...) makes a true copy of a row. Writing g[r] = oranges[r] only copies the slice header, so both grids would share the same cells.
Process the queue one level at a time: take the whole current wave, build the next wave, then add one minute. Adding a minute per orange popped gives a far too big answer.

recap.key: Queue all rotten oranges together. Each full wave rots its fresh neighbours and costs one minute. Fresh left over means -1.
recap.complexity: Time O(rows x cols). Space O(rows x cols).
moves: Queue every rotten orange, count the fresh
Rot all neighbours of the current wave, add a minute
Stop when no fresh is left or the queue is empty
Return minutes, or -1 if fresh remain
